chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Mufazzal ibn Salih, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The Trustworthy Spirit informed me that Allah, there is no god but He, when He halts the creatures and gathers the first and the last, Hell will be brought, led by a thousand reins. Each rein is held by a hundred thousand angels from the strong and harsh ones. It has a roaring, crushing, sighing, and inhalation sound. And indeed, it sighs a sigh, and if Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had not delayed it until the Reckoning, it would have destroyed everyone. Then a neck would emerge from it, encompassing the creatures, the righteous among them and the sinners. So there is no creature of Allah, a servant from His servants, angel, or prophet, except that he calls out, "O Lord, my soul, my soul!" And You say, "O Lord, my community, my community!"

Then a Bridge is placed over it, thinner than hair and sharper than a sword. Upon it are three hurdles: the first is Trustworthiness and Mercy, the second is Salat (Prayer), and the third is the Lord of the Worlds, there is no god but Him. They are tasked with crossing it. Mercy and Trustworthiness hold them back. If they are saved from it, Salat holds them back. If they are saved from it, the destination is the Lord of the Worlds, Majestic is His Mention. And this is the Statement of Allah, Blessed and High: 'Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful.'

And the people are upon the Bridge; some clinging, their feet slipping, and their feet firm. The angels around it call out: 'O Generous! O Forbearing! Excuse and Pardon, and Return by Your Grace, and Secure.' And the people flock upon it like moths. So when one is saved by the Mercy of Allah, Blessed and High, he looks at it and says: 'Praise is to Allah Who saved me from you after despair, by His Grace and Favor. Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving, Appreciative.'
ai.seo_question: What are the stages of crossing the Bridge (Sirat) on the Day of Judgment according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi elaborates on the eschatological mechanics of the Day of Judgment, highlighting the immense scale of Hell being led by a hundred thousand angels and the intricate, multi-stage crossing of the Sirat bridge. It underscores the Shia theological emphasis on divine mercy and intercession, where attributes like Trustworthiness (Al-Amanah) and Mercy act as filters before the final judgment, reflecting the Quranic concept of God being 'on the lookout' for His servants.
